Malignant Peripheral Nerve Sheath Tumor: The presence of S-100 protein and HMB-45 positivity, combined with the clinical and radiological features, points towards a nerve sheath tumor, and the absence of melanin and the clinical presentation suggest MPNST. The histological features, including compact nests and fascicles with large rounded and spindle-shaped cells, pleomorphic nuclei, and moderately numerous mitoses, also support this diagnosis.
Other Soft Tissue Sarcomas: Although the presence of EMA and cytokeratins can help differentiate between various types of soft tissue tumors, the clinical and radiological features, combined with the histological features, make MPNST the most likely diagnosis. Other soft tissue sarcomas, such as leiomyosarcoma or liposarcoma, are less likely given the specific immunohistochemical stains and histological features presented.
